articles.title: Broadcom To Lend Anthropic Up To $42 Billion To Finance AI Infrastructure
articles.snippet:
Broadcom has agreed to provide Anthropic with up to $42 billion in financing to support the AI company's massive infrastructure expansion, according to Anthropic's IPO filing reviewed by Reuters. The financing could cover roughly one-third of Anthropic's $125.2 billion commitment to lease tensor processing unit (TPU) computing capacity over five years.
The post Broadcom To Lend Anthropic Up To $42 Billion To Finance AI Infrastructure appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Broadcom To Lend Anthropic Up To $42 Billion To Finance AI Infrastructure
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 1, 2026
Broadcom To Lend Anthropic Up To $42 Billion To Finance AI Infrastructure
Broadcom has agreed to provide Anthropic with up to $42 billion in financing to support the AI company’s massive infrastructure expansion, according to Anthropic’s IPO filing reviewed by Reuters . The financing could cover roughly one-third of Anthropic’s $125.2 billion commitment to lease tensor processing unit (TPU) computing capacity over five years.
The arrangement highlights the increasingly close relationship between Anthropic and Broadcom, which spans chip supply, equipment leasing and financing. Broadcom is expected to become Anthropic’s largest compute supplier in 2027 as the AI company expands the infrastructure required to train and operate its Claude models.
Under the financing agreement, Broadcom can designate a financing partner, and Anthropic could convert debt instruments into equity. Anthropic said in its filing that it does not expect to sell any of the notes before completing its planned initial public offering.
The financing comes as Anthropic prepares for an IPO that could potentially value the company at about $2 trillion, according to Reuters. The company’s extensive spending commitments show the enormous capital requirements of developing frontier AI models and building the infrastructure needed to run them at scale.
Anthropic’s $125.2 billion TPU commitment covers a five-year lease of computing capacity. Google and Broadcom have collaborated on multiple generations of Google’s TPUs, specialized processors designed for artificial intelligence workloads.
Anthropic announced an expanded partnership with Broadcom and Google in April 2026 that is expected to give the company access to multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU computing capacity beginning in 2027.
The relationship could also create a significant new revenue stream for Broadcom. Anthropic is expected to become Broadcom’s largest compute customer in 2027, while Broadcom projects approximately $115 billion of AI semiconductor revenue in fiscal 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal 2028.
The financing strategy resembles moves by Nvidia, which has increasingly used its balance sheet and investments to help customers finance AI infrastructure containing its chips. Broadcom’s arrangement with Anthropic similarly connects financing with future demand for its semiconductor technology.
Anthropic also identified risks associated with the relationship. In its IPO prospectus, the company said Broadcom’s roles as both a hardware supplier and financing partner could create “potential conflicts of interest” affecting Anthropic’s access to computing infrastructure.
Broadcom’s decisions involving hardware availability and pricing could potentially influence Anthropic’s ability to secure enough computing capacity to support its operations.
Anthropic disclosed that it deposited cash into a restricted account for Broadcom’s benefit in April 2026 under the convertible debt arrangement. Under certain circumstances, the company could be required to contribute additional amounts to that account.
The filing also warned that certain payment or performance defaults could make a substantial portion of Anthropic’s lease obligations immediately payable, while potentially limiting the company’s ability to use the $42 billion Broadcom financing facility to satisfy those obligations.

articles.title: Etched fields funding offers at $40B+ valuation, sources say
articles.snippet: Etched fields funding offers at $40B+ valuation, sources say TechCrunch
articles.text:
Although it’s only been a couple of months since Etched raised $700 million at a $21 billion valuation , the AI chip startup is already being plied with investment offers at double or more its value, according to people familiar with the company.
Etched is reviewing incoming bids that range from $40 billion from top-tier investors to $50 billion from lesser-known backers, one person said. These fundraising talks are early, so terms of any deal, should one happen, may change. Etched declined to comment.
While this may seem like a fast timetable to raise another mega round, Etched is pursuing a particularly expensive segment of the AI industry: building full AI hardware systems powered by its own proprietary chips. The person familiar with these offers said that if it raises as much as its last round, this could give Etched a cushion of as much as 3.5 years of runway.
There are reasons why VCs are hot to own a piece of Etched. The four-year-old startup shows promise of challenging Nvidia. Not only did quant trading firm Jane Street lead the last $700 million round, it is also a customer that took delivery of an early system. Etched said in July that it had already secured $1 billion in customer orders, including the one from Jane Street, after manufacturing its test chip at a TSMC factory this summer.
Co-founder and COO Robert Wachen previously told TechCrunch that investors are so enthusiastic because Etched has designed two new components from scratch to speed up inference — the computing process that happens after a user submits a prompt.
The company claims its chips can process more tokens faster and at a lower cost than Nvidia’s. That’s the reason its processors have been so attractive to Jane Street, for whom a microscopic advantage in speed can yield massive profits.
The startup has also impressed investors with its ability to attract engineers from Nvidia, with roughly 15% of Etched’s 400-person workforce having previously worked at the chip giant, according to The Wall Street Journal.
Etched also operates a new 10-megawatt data center in Silicon Valley and established a facility in Taiwan to coordinate production near TSMC.
Co-founders Gavin Uberti and Chris Zhu famously met in an advanced math course at Harvard, while Wachen was Uberti’s roommate and they dropped out to pursue the company.
In terms of fast rounds at big leaps in valuations, Etched already has a history of them. The startup announced a $300 million round at a $10.3 billion valuation led by Sequoia in July. It announced the $700 million round at a $21 billion valuation in September. Back-to-back funding rounds, which essentially act as a single financing split into two tranches with separate valuations, are increasingly common among the buzziest startups.

articles.title: SpaceX Reportedly Seeking $40 Billion Financing To Buy Nvidia AI Chips
articles.snippet:
SpaceX is seeking approximately $40 billion in financing to purchase Nvidia artificial intelligence chips, with the Elon Musk-led company discussing the potential financing with banks and asset managers, according to a Reuters report. The proposed financing would consist of approximately $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion of investment-grade debt.
The post SpaceX Reportedly Seeking $40 Billion Financing To Buy Nvidia AI Chips appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
SpaceX Reportedly Seeking $40 Billion Financing To Buy Nvidia AI Chips
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
SpaceX Reportedly Seeking $40 Billion Financing To Buy Nvidia AI Chips
SpaceX is seeking approximately $40 billion in financing to purchase Nvidia artificial intelligence chips, with the Elon Musk-led company discussing the potential financing with banks and asset managers, according to a Reuters report . The proposed financing would consist of approximately $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion of investment-grade debt.
Asset manager PIMCO is among the parties SpaceX has been discussing financing with, while Apollo is expected to lead the transaction and help distribute the debt to a broad group of investors.
The financing would support SpaceX’s purchase of Nvidia hardware as Musk expands the computing infrastructure supporting his companies’ artificial intelligence ambitions.
Musk recently said xAI’s Colossus 2 data center could more than double the number of Nvidia chips it uses by December. He also said the company plans to rely exclusively on Nvidia hardware when building its data centers.
The potential $40 billion financing illustrates the rapidly increasing capital requirements associated with building large-scale AI infrastructure as technology companies compete for advanced GPUs, power, data center capacity and networking equipment.
Morgan Stanley estimates the broader AI infrastructure market will require approximately $1.5 trillion of external financing by 2028, even as banks and other investors become more selective about underwriting large AI-related projects.
Nvidia has also been working with major financial institutions to expand the pool of capital available for AI infrastructure.
In August, Nvidia partnered with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR on financing platforms intended to mobilize more than $500 billion for AI infrastructure projects.
The financing effort also highlights the increasingly close relationship between AI computing demand and credit markets.
Advanced Nvidia GPUs represent one of the largest capital expenses for companies building frontier AI systems, while the scale of new clusters increasingly requires financing structures more commonly associated with major infrastructure projects.

articles.title: Intesa Sanpaolo’s €35 Billion MPS Bid Wins Backing From Largest Shareholder Delfin
articles.snippet:
Intesa Sanpaolo's improved €35 billion ($39 billion) takeover bid for Monte dei Paschi di Siena has secured the support of MPS’s largest shareholder, Delfin, according to Reuters.
The post Intesa Sanpaolo’s €35 Billion MPS Bid Wins Backing From Largest Shareholder Delfin appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Intesa Sanpaolo’s €35 Billion MPS Bid Wins Backing From Largest Shareholder Delfin
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
Intesa Sanpaolo’s €35 Billion MPS Bid Wins Backing From Largest Shareholder Delfin
Intesa Sanpaolo’s improved €35 billion ($39 billion) takeover bid for Monte dei Paschi di Siena has secured the support of MPS’s largest shareholder, Delfin, according to Reuters .
Delfin, which owns a 17.6% stake in MPS, has committed to tendering its shares into Intesa’s cash-and-stock offer and voting against a defensive strategy proposed by MPS Chief Executive Luigi Lovaglio.
The support represents an important development for Intesa because Delfin had previously been viewed as a key ally of Lovaglio.
MPS shareholders are scheduled to vote on October 29 on the bank’s defense strategy. Lovaglio needs support from two-thirds of shareholders for the plan to proceed.
Intesa recently increased the cash portion of its offer by another €800 million, raising the cash component by 25%. The enhancement increases the overall value of the bid by approximately 2.3% based on MPS’s October 2 closing price.
Under the revised terms, Intesa is offering €1.25 in cash plus 1.6 newly issued Intesa shares for each MPS share tendered.
Intesa has warned that it intends to withdraw its offer if MPS shareholders approve the defense strategy.
MPS has also been pursuing a plan to take Mediobanca private and merge the business into MPS. That proposal is also expected to go before shareholders on October 29.
Intesa has said it would retain approximately half of MPS’s branch network to address competition concerns while keeping MPS’s holdings in Mediobanca and Generali.
The proposed takeover comes amid a broader period of consolidation across Italy’s banking sector, with Intesa entering the contest for MPS after the lender had itself acquired control of Mediobanca and become a major shareholder in insurer Generali.

This list covers fintech startups that closed a disclosed round between June and October 2026, at Series C or earlier, and published at least one traction figure. Seven companies qualified, from an AI accounting platform valued at $1 billion to a Riyadh-based SME lender.
The capital behind them is concentrated. Fintech startups raised $28.6 billion worldwide in the first half of 2026, up 22.7% year over year, while deal count fell 25.7% to 1,605 rounds, according to Crunchbase.

Fintech startups funding in 2026: totals and deal counts
Crunchbase counted $28.6 billion in fintech venture funding in H1 2026. That was 17.3% below the $34.6 billion raised in H2 2025, the sector’s strongest half-year since late 2022.
Fewer, larger rounds drove the annual gain. Spread across 1,605 deals, the H1 2026 total works out to about $17.8 million per round. The same data implies about $23.3 billion across 2,161 deals in H1 2025, or about $10.8 million per round. Average check size rose 65%.
US companies took $15 billion, more than 52% of the global total. The UK followed with $2.7 billion.
The US raised 5.6 times as much as the UK, which took 9.4% of H1 funding. That left about $10.9 billion, or 38.1%, for every other country combined.
FinTech Global publishes quarterly totals that run higher than Crunchbase’s, because its tracker counts a wider set of deals that includes insurtech and cybersecurity companies. articles.title: RTX’s Raytheon Awarded Up To $24.4 Billion Contract For SM-6 Interceptors
articles.snippet:
Raytheon, an RTX business, has secured a multi-year contract valued at up to $24.4 billion for Standard Missile-6 interceptors, significantly expanding long-term production of the missile system for the U.S. Navy.
The post RTX’s Raytheon Awarded Up To $24.4 Billion Contract For SM-6 Interceptors appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
RTX’s Raytheon Awarded Up To $24.4 Billion Contract For SM-6 Interceptors
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 1, 2026
RTX’s Raytheon Awarded Up To $24.4 Billion Contract For SM-6 Interceptors
Raytheon, an RTX business, has secured a multi-year contract valued at up to $24.4 billion for Standard Missile-6 interceptors, significantly expanding long-term production of the missile system for the U.S. Navy.
The agreement covers five years and includes two additional option years, giving Raytheon a potential seven-year production framework for SM-6 interceptors.
The contract is designed to provide the U.S. Navy with a more consistent and reliable supply of SM-6 missiles as demand increases for weapons capable of supporting both offensive and defensive missions.
The new order builds on previous long-term production agreements between Raytheon and the Department of War and represents a major effort to increase the availability of one of the Navy’s key missile systems.
SM-6 is designed to perform several missions from a common missile platform, including anti-air warfare, anti-surface warfare and ballistic missile defense.
Raytheon describes SM-6 as the only combat-proven weapon capable of performing all three missions.
The missile has been successfully fired from multiple U.S. Navy ship-based platforms as well as land-based launchers, giving military operators flexibility in how the system is deployed against different types of threats.
The size and duration of the contract also provide Raytheon and its suppliers with greater visibility into future demand, supporting investments intended to increase manufacturing capacity.
Raytheon has been expanding its skilled workforce, strengthening relationships with suppliers throughout the defense industrial base and introducing additional automation into its manufacturing operations.
Those investments are intended to remove production constraints and support substantially higher SM-6 output for both near-term and longer-term requirements.
The SM-6 agreement follows other major multi-year missile production awards for Raytheon as the company and the U.S. government work to expand munitions production capacity.
Raytheon’s missile portfolio spans integrated air and missile defense, precision weapons, interceptors, hypersonic technologies and other systems used across land, air, sea and space.
RTX employs more than 180,000 people globally and generated more than $88 billion in sales in 2025.
KEY QUOTE:
“SM-6’s multi-mission capability is vital to our customer, and Raytheon is intensely focused on meeting the demand. By continuously investing in our operations and facilities, we are removing constraints and boosting capacity to ensure we deliver this critical capability our sailors depend on.”
Phil Jasper, President of Raytheon

articles.snippet:
GlobalFoundries has been selected as the technology provider and operator for two new semiconductor manufacturing facilities at its Malta, New York, campus under a U.S.-Japan initiative providing up to $21 billion in funding. Pasted markdown The initiative stems from a U.S.-Japan trade and investment agreement and is designed to expand semiconductor manufacturing capacity in the […]
The post GlobalFoundries To Operate Two New York Semiconductor Fabs Under Up To $21 Billion U.S.-Japan Initiative appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
GlobalFoundries To Operate Two New York Semiconductor Fabs Under Up To $21 Billion U.S.-Japan Initiative
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 14, 2026
GlobalFoundries To Operate Two New York Semiconductor Fabs Under Up To $21 Billion U.S.-Japan Initiative
GlobalFoundries has been selected as the technology provider and operator for two new semiconductor manufacturing facilities at its Malta, New York, campus under a U.S.-Japan initiative providing up to $21 billion in funding. Pasted markdown
The initiative stems from a U.S.-Japan trade and investment agreement and is designed to expand semiconductor manufacturing capacity in the United States while strengthening supply chains serving automotive, industrial, connected infrastructure, and other markets.
Japan will provide the investment, while GlobalFoundries will contribute its semiconductor technologies, manufacturing expertise, and operational capabilities.
An initial investment of approximately $10 billion is expected to accelerate construction of a new 300mm semiconductor fab scheduled to come online in 2029.
An additional investment of approximately $10 billion would fund construction of a second fab at the Malta site.
The first facility is expected to add approximately 900,000 300mm wafers of annual U.S. manufacturing capacity when fully operational. A second fab would add approximately the same amount.
GlobalFoundries expects the broader project to create approximately 27,000 construction and semiconductor ecosystem jobs along with more than 1,000 high-skilled manufacturing jobs in New York’s Capital Region.
The company plans to break ground on the first fab later in 2026. GlobalFoundries said the Malta site is already permitted and shovel-ready, allowing the project to use existing infrastructure to accelerate construction.
Separately, GlobalFoundries agreed with the U.S. Department of Commerce to amend its existing CHIPS and Science Act award and reallocate $955 million to accelerate investments in silicon photonics, silicon-germanium technology, and advanced packaging.
The company will make those investments at its facilities in Malta and Burlington, Vermont, to increase U.S. manufacturing capacity for technologies used in communications infrastructure and data centers.
Under a separate agreement, the U.S. Department of Commerce will receive an equity interest of approximately 4% in GlobalFoundries.
The expansion also builds on GlobalFoundries’ relationships with customers and semiconductor industry partners in the United States and Japan.
Renesas said it is planning around the new New York capacity as an extension of its own production footprint, while Tokyo Electron expects to support the expanded semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem.
Apple also highlighted its existing relationship with GlobalFoundries to manufacture chips for Apple products in the United States, while Cirrus Logic said the new facilities will provide access to additional domestic capacity for next-generation mixed-signal products.
General Motors said the additional domestic manufacturing capacity could support a stronger semiconductor supply chain as vehicles require greater processing power for technologies including centralized computing, artificial intelligence, autonomy, and software-defined vehicle systems.

articles.title: IBM Reports Q3 2026 Revenue Of $17.1 Billion, Net Income Of $2.2 Billion, And Raises Free Cash Flow Outlook
articles.snippet:
IBM reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $17.1 billion, an increase of 5% year over year and 6% at constant currency, supported by growth in its Software and Infrastructure businesses. The technology company also reported net income from continuing operations of $2.2 billion, up 26% from the prior year, as demand for enterprise software, artificial intelligence capabilities, and infrastructure solutions supported its financial performance.
The post IBM Reports Q3 2026 Revenue Of $17.1 Billion, Net Income Of $2.2 Billion, And Raises Free Cash Flow Outlook appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
IBM Reports Q3 2026 Revenue Of $17.1 Billion, Net Income Of $2.2 Billion, And Raises Free Cash Flow Outlook
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
IBM Reports Q3 2026 Revenue Of $17.1 Billion, Net Income Of $2.2 Billion, And Raises Free Cash Flow Outlook
IBM reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $17.1 billion, an increase of 5% year over year and 6% at constant currency, supported by growth in its Software and Infrastructure businesses. The technology company also reported net income from continuing operations of $2.2 billion, up 26% from the prior year, as demand for enterprise software, artificial intelligence capabilities, and infrastructure solutions supported its financial performance.
IBM reported diluted earnings per share from continuing operations of $2.31, up 26% from $1.84 in the third quarter of 2025. On an operating non-GAAP basis, diluted earnings per share increased 11% to $2.95, compared with $2.65 a year earlier.
Gross profit increased to $9.7 billion, although the GAAP gross profit margin declined 50 basis points to 56.8%. Operating gross margin was 58.5%, compared with 58.7% in the prior-year quarter.
IBM’s GAAP pretax income reached approximately $2.5 billion, representing a pretax margin of 14.6%. Operating non-GAAP pretax income rose 9% to $3.3 billion, and the operating pretax margin improved 70 basis points to 19.3%.
The company’s Software division generated $7.8 billion in quarterly revenue, an increase of 8% as reported and 9% at constant currency. Software remained IBM’s largest operating segment, benefiting from continued demand for hybrid cloud, data management, and enterprise transaction processing solutions.
Within Software, Red Hat revenue increased 11%, while Data revenue grew 19%, or 20% at constant currency. Transaction Processing revenue rose 9%, reflecting demand for enterprise systems that support mission-critical business operations.
Automation revenue declined 3%, partially offsetting growth elsewhere in the division.
Software segment profit reached approximately $2.7 billion, compared with $2.4 billion in the third quarter of 2025. The segment’s profit margin improved to 35% from 32.9%, reflecting stronger operating performance.
IBM Consulting generated $5.3 billion in quarterly revenue, remaining broadly flat year over year on a reported basis and increasing 2% at constant currency.
Within Consulting, Strategy and Technology revenue rose 2% (4% at constant currency), while Intelligent Operations revenue fell 2%.
The Consulting segment reported profit of $653 million, compared with $686 million a year earlier, with its profit margin declining to 12.2% from 12.9%.
IBM Infrastructure reported revenue of $3.7 billion, up 4% and 5% at constant currency.
Hybrid Infrastructure revenue increased 8%, supported by particularly strong performance in Distributed Infrastructure, where revenue rose 31%, or 32% at constant currency.
IBM Z revenue declined 20%, while Infrastructure Support revenue decreased 3%. Despite those declines, the Infrastructure segment increased profit to $715 million from $644 million, with its profit margin improving to 19.3%.
The Financing segment generated $192 million in revenue, down 4% year over year.
Cash generation was another significant component of IBM’s quarterly performance. The company reported $4 billion in net cash provided by operating activities, an increase of approximately $900 million from the prior-year quarter.

articles.title: DeepSeek reportedly raises $15B days after US restrictions
articles.snippet: DeepSeek has reportedly raised $15 billion in one of China's largest funding rounds, just days after the U.S. ordered federal agencies to remove its technology over national security concerns.
articles.text:
In Brief
Posted:
6:11 AM PDT · October 22, 2026
Image Credits: GREG BAKER/AFP / Getty Images
Kate Park
DeepSeek reportedly raises $15B days after US restrictions
Just two days after the U.S. ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek’s AI technology from their systems over security concerns, the Chinese AI lab has raised about $15 billion, about 100 billion yuan, one of the biggest funding rounds in the country, Bloomberg reported.
Potential investors include Chinese battery maker CATL and Tencent, the company behind WeChat, among others, according to the report.
The reported funding follows DeepSeek’s investment round in June, when it raised more than $7 billion at a valuation of $50 billion. The company was also reportedly seeking an additional $1.5 billion at a valuation of around $71 billion in July , with plans for a potential IPO in China as early as next year.
The Hangzhou-based AI startup is ramping up spending on AI infrastructure and open models for domestic and international markets, even as it faces restrictions in the U.S., the report said. Its expansion could further intensify competition among domestic rivals.
The massive funding round is the latest sign of investors pouring billions into AI companies around the world, including those in China, to compete in the global AI race. Chinese company Kimi developer Moonshot AI secured $2 billion at a $20 billion valuation in May. Manus AI raised more than $500 million earlier this month. Meanwhile, Chinese companies Zhipu AI (Z.ai) and MiniMax, which both went public in Hong Kong in January, have market capitalizations of roughly $29 billion and $7.2 billion , respectively, as of today.
DeepSeek was founded in 2023 by Liang Wenfeng , who previously co-founded Chinese quantitative hedge fund High-Flyer, which helped finance DeepSeek’s early development. The AI startup gained global attention in early 2025 with its free-to-use, open-weight RI reasoning model, challenging the dominance of U.S. AI companies. Liang retains an estimated 81.6% stake in its Chinese operating entity following its earlier funding round, according to corporate ownership data analyzed by WireScreen.
DeepSeek did not immediately respond to a TechCrunch request for comment.

articles.title: Jabil Reports Q4 Revenue Of $10.6 Billion And FY2026 Revenue Of $36 Billion
articles.snippet:
Jabil reported preliminary fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 net revenue of $10.6 billion as the manufacturing services company closed a year marked by strong growth in AI infrastructure and other end markets.
The post Jabil Reports Q4 Revenue Of $10.6 Billion And FY2026 Revenue Of $36 Billion appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Jabil Reports Q4 Revenue Of $10.6 Billion And FY2026 Revenue Of $36 Billion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 1, 2026
Jabil Reports Q4 Revenue Of $10.6 Billion And FY2026 Revenue Of $36 Billion
Jabil reported preliminary fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 net revenue of $10.6 billion as the manufacturing services company closed a year marked by strong growth in AI infrastructure and other end markets.
For the quarter ended August 31, 2026, Jabil generated U.S. GAAP operating income of $602 million and GAAP diluted earnings per share of $3.76. Core operating income was $675 million, while core diluted earnings per share reached $4.40.
For the full fiscal year, net revenue reached $36.0 billion, representing 21% growth. GAAP operating income totaled $1.7 billion and GAAP diluted EPS was $9.75. Core operating income reached $2.1 billion, with core diluted EPS of $13.09.
Jabil also generated more than $1.5 billion of adjusted free cash flow during fiscal 2026 while expanding its core operating margin by 40 basis points.
The company said growth was supported by increasing demand for AI infrastructure along with strength across automotive, healthcare, energy infrastructure, defense and aerospace, and warehouse and retail automation.
For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Jabil expects net revenue between $10.6 billion and $11.4 billion. GAAP operating income is projected between $481 million and $541 million, with GAAP diluted EPS ranging from $2.78 to $3.18.
Core first-quarter operating income is expected between $592 million and $652 million, with core diluted EPS between $3.80 and $4.20.
For the full 2027 fiscal year, Jabil expects revenue of $44.5 billion, which would represent approximately 24% growth. The company forecasts a core operating margin of 6.1%, up approximately 30 basis points, and core diluted EPS of $17.55, representing projected growth of 34%.
Adjusted free cash flow for fiscal 2027 is expected to be approximately $1.6 billion.
Jabil said the outlook reflects expanding customer relationships and committed business supporting newly added capacity. The company continues to take on more engineering, supply chain and manufacturing responsibilities for customers while maintaining what it describes as an asset-light operating model.
Jabil operates more than 100 sites globally and provides engineering, supply chain and manufacturing services across a broad range of industries.
